analysis.brief_en: The article highlights three key issues in the medical field. First, it reports that physicians believe media coverage of hantavirus is exaggerated, with 85% perceiving the risk as overstated and 77% rating the population risk as low or non-meaningful. Second, it details a $2 billion telemedicine fraud scheme involving fraudulent prescriptions and sham visits, which was uncovered between 2017 and 2022. The scheme targeted U.S. insurers and involved over 75 locations, with private insurers paying out more than $758 million. Three individuals were sentenced, while the alleged leader remains at large. Third, a study by Ohio State University found that nearly 1 in 10 surgeons leave the profession within 8 years, with attrition rates spiking in 2020 during the pandemic. The research noted mid-career departures as the highest and a decline in rural representation. The article emphasizes the disconnect between media attention and actual risk, as well as the impact of the pandemic on surgeon retention.

news.content: Internacional| EN 28 de agosto de 2026 ArgentinaBrasilEcuadorEspañaInternacionalMexicoPanamaPeru EN AgroAnalysisCruisesCurrent AffairsEnvironment and EnergyForeign TradeLogisticsPortsShipbuildingShipping Inicio/Cruises Cruises > Deadly Hantavirus Cruise Saga Nears End as Final Passengers Leave Ship The final six passengers of the hantavirus-hit MV Hondius were disembarking off Tenerife on May 11, concluding a complex evacuation operation that has repatriated 94 people across 41 days. The World Health Organization confirmed seven cases of the Andes strain of hantavirus with three deaths—a Dutch couple and a German national—while health officials emphasized the virus poses little risk to the general population due to limited person-to-person transmission. 11 de mayo de 2026 • 4 min de lectura 11 de mayo de 2026 • 4 min de lectura Deadly Hantavirus Cruise Saga Nears End as Final Passengers Leave Ship SANTA CRUZ DE TENERIFE, Spain, May 11 (Reuters) – The last six passengers and some of the crew of the hantavirus-hit MV Hondius anchored off Tenerife were readying to disembark on Monday as the ship's captain praised their patience and discipline during an "extremely challenging" few weeks. The final passengers – four Australians, one Briton who lives in Australia and a New Zealander – were waiting to be taken off the MV Hondius, a polar expedition ship, in small boats for transfer to Tenerife where a flight would take them to the Netherlands to spend time in quarantine. Nineteen crew members from the ship and three doctors who treated them were due to take off for the Netherlands on an earlier flight, the Dutch Foreign Ministry said. The MV Hondius was then due to continue its journey with 26 crew members to the Netherlands – its flag state – where it would be disinfected, health authorities said. "I could not imagine sailing through these circumstances with a better group of people, guests and crew alike," Captain Jan Dobrogowski, from the Netherlands, said in a video posted on Oceanwide Expeditions' website. The disembarkation caps a complex operation that has so far resulted in 94 people being evacuated and repatriated to their countries of residence, 41 days after the MV Hondius set off from southern Argentina and nine days after the first positive test result for the respiratory viral infection. Three people have died since the start of the outbreak – a Dutch couple and a German national. The World Health Organization said on Monday there were now seven confirmed cases of the Andes strain of hantavirus, and two other suspected cases – one who died before being tested, and one on Tristan da Cunha, a remote South Atlantic island where there were no tests available. FRENCH WOMAN'S CONDITION DETERIORATING The confirmed cases include a French passenger, who tested positive after the ship docked in the Canary Islands on Sunday. Her condition is deteriorating, French Health Minister Stephanie Rist said. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services said one of the 17 Americans being repatriated had also tested mildly positive for the Andes virus. The Spanish Health Ministry said a test of another sample of the American at a different lab had been inconclusive. A second American also had mild symptoms. As the MV Hondius approached the Canary Islands late last week amid protests from the regional government about the risk of the virus spreading, Spain's health minister and the WHO had said all passengers were "asymptomatic." Results of tests on 14 Spanish passengers currently quarantining at a military hospital in Madrid were due later on Monday, Spain's Health Ministry added. 'THIS IS NOT COVID' The virus is usually spread by wild rodents but also transmittable person-to-person in rare cases of close contact. However, health officials say that because the virus does not spread easily between people, there is little risk to the general population, urging calm to a public scarred from the experience of the COVID-19 pandemic. The MV Hondius had been carrying 147 passengers and crew from 23 countries when a cluster of severe respiratory illnesses among passengers was first reported to the WHO on May 3. By then, 34 other passengers had disembarked on islands in the Atlantic before the cruise ship headed north to Cape Verde, where news of the outbreak emerged. It was first detected by health officials in Johannesburg on May 2 treating a British man who disembarked the ship. That was some three weeks after the first passenger, a Dutchman, had died. The luxury cruise ship left for Spain's Canary Islands on May 6 after Madrid had accepted a WHO request to manage its evacuation. The WHO has recommended a 42-day quarantine for all passengers, its director of epidemic and pandemic management, Maria Van Kerkhove, told a briefing. On Monday, the head of the Italian pharmaceutical lobby, Marcello Cattani, told a conference in Milan there was little need to develop a hantavirus vaccine. "Only a small number of citizens, fortunately, are involved," he said. "The path to achieving a vaccine is absolutely feasible, but we are confident there will be no need for one because it will not go from an outbreak to an epidemic or a pandemic." news.content: Kodu E-post Äri Failid Foto Reklaam Veel E-post Äri Failid Foto Tutvumine Kalender Mängud Kontaktid Shortlink Uudised Hangi Preemium EE Eesti English Latviešu Русский Lietuvių Español Français Deutsch Kõik Maailmas Krimi Sport Showbiz Naistele Tehnika More Kõik Maailmas Krimi Sport Showbiz Naistele Tehnika Kodu & aed Kultuur Äri Reisimine More Maailmas Inside the science of hantavirus transmission: 'Virus not known for human-to-human transmission' 4. mai 2026 Nadia Massih is pleased to welcome Adam Taylor, Professor of Anatomy at Lancaster University. Global health fears can spread faster than viruses themselves, and so clarity becomes as vital as containment. Professor Taylor, a specialist in the hantavirus, offers an evidence-based perspective on a concerning outbreak aboard a cruise ship near Cape Verde. Balancing scientific rigor with public concern, the professor resists alarmism. He underscores that “this virus is not known for human-to-human transmission” and insists that “the risk is incredibly low,” even as investigations continue. Maailmas CIA Chief in Moscow Gave a 'Gloomy Assessment' of Russia's Situation - NYT 28. aug 2026 CIA Director John Ratcliffe, during his visit to Moscow on August 25, shared with the head of the Federal Security Service (FSB), Alexander Bortnikov, "his gloomy assessment" of Russia's situation in the war in Ukraine and urged Moscow to start negotiations before the military and economic situation worsens even further. This was reported on Thursday, August 27, by The New York Times (NYT), citing current and former U.S. officials. Some of the newspaper's sources explained Bortnikov's selection as an intermediary in communication with Russian President Vladimir Putin by stating that the Russian leader, as a former intelligence officer, would perceive information from the CIA director as more trustworthy than data coming through regular diplomatic channels. NYT also reported that the communication channel between Ratcliffe and Bortnikov operates independently of others. ## ## Ratcliffe Informed Bortnikov About Heavy Losses and Slow Progress of the Russian Army As NYT points out, CIA officials doubt that Putin is being provided with reliable information about the course of the war and the scale of losses of the Russian army. The content of the message Ratcliffe conveyed to Bortnikov is not disclosed by the newspaper, but it notes that it "echoed some public statements" made by the CIA director. For instance, in July, Ratcliffe stated that over the past year and a half, Russia has captured only about 1% of Ukrainian territory, attributing this to the successful development of the UAV sector in the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU). Additionally, he claimed that the life expectancy of a Russian soldier on the front line does not exceed 35 minutes. At the same time, the CIA director did not voice threats about possible consequences if Putin ignores the message from the U.S. and does not cease hostilities during his meeting with the FSB head. It is also noted that before meeting with Bortnikov, Ratcliffe spoke with representatives of Ukraine, assuring them that he intended to explore Moscow's position rather than negotiate concessions on behalf of Kyiv. ## ## Versions of the Purpose of John Ratcliffe's Visit to Moscow Vary Ratcliffe arrived in Russia aboard a U.S. Air Force Boeing C-17 Globemaster III transport aircraft on August 25, and just a few hours later left the country. The Washington Post claimed that the CIA chief's visit was related to "contacts between intelligence agencies." Later, Politico, citing three sources, stated that the primary purpose of Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow was to convey a message to the Russian side about the inadmissibility of attacking U.S. NATO allies, particularly concerning Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania. Russian President's Press Secretary Dmitry Peskov, commenting on Ratcliffe's visit, said that he did not hold meetings with the head of state. The head of the Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), Sergey Naryshkin, confirmed his meeting with the CIA chief but emphasized that there was "nothing unusual" about it. U.S. President Donald Trump also referred to Ratcliffe's trip to Moscow as "a routine matter," noting that he meets with Naryshkin "once every six months or once a year." Maailmas Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to 'Lake America' as Carney pushes back 27. aug 2026 US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order to update the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" in the country's geographic naming service. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney pushed back, citing the name's Indigenous origins, as the row between the neighbors roiled on. Maailmas Latest news bulletin | August 28th, 2026 – Morning 28. aug 2026 Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this August 28th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel. Maailmas Canada's Prime Minister Responds to Trump Regarding Lake Ontario 28. aug 2026 Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney criticized U.S. President Donald Trump's decision to rename Lake Ontario - the smallest of the five Great Lakes located on the border of the two countries - to "Lake America." The order to change the name of the body of water was signed by the American leader at the White House on Thursday, July 27, just a few days after the collapse of a trade deal with Canada. "We are immediately changing the name of Lake Ontario to 'Lake America,'" Trump said to reporters. He explained his decision by stating that "Canadian officials treated U.S. representatives very poorly." Carney reacted to the American leader's decision. "This name has been in use for over 400 years; it emerged long before the formation of the Canadian Confederation and the adoption of the U.S. Declaration of Independence. We know that America is changing. Its trade relations, foreign policy, national monuments, and even hydronyms are changing. Canadians know that to call things by their names means to call this lake Lake Ontario. That has been the case, that is the case, and that will always be the case," the Canadian Prime Minister wrote on his social media page X. ## ## Trump Renamed the Lake After the Collapse of the Trade Deal and Canada's Retaliatory Tariffs Trump first announced plans to rename Lake Ontario on August 25 - three days after the U.S. imposed a 50% tariff on a range of goods from Canada due to the collapse of negotiations for a new trade deal: among other things, on wine, furniture, dairy products, cement, clothing, fishing rods, and hockey equipment. Immediately after this, Carney announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on a range of goods from the U.S. According to media reports, they will affect sectors such as dairy, metallurgy, household appliances, pulp and paper, electronics, and others. The tariffs are expected to take effect on September 8. Both sides blamed each other for the collapse of the trade deal. Carney stated that an agreement could not be reached due to the last-minute changes proposed by the U.S. that were "unfair, non-market, and called into question the reliability of any deal." U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, who participated in the negotiations, said that Ottawa "refused to finalize the trade deal on the terms agreed upon earlier that week." ## ## Trump Repeatedly Proposes Renaming Geographic Features and Institutions Since the beginning of his second term, Trump has repeatedly proposed renaming major geographic features and various institutions. In January 2025, at his initiative, the Gulf of Mexico was renamed the American Gulf, and the Denali Mountains in Alaska were renamed back to McKinley. The first decision in Mexico was criticized, noting that the previous name had been used in international navigation for many centuries. In December 2025, the name of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington was supplemented with Trump's name. In May 2026, a court ruled to remove the current U.S. president's name from the title. The judge justified his verdict, in particular, by stating that the name was assigned to the center by the U.S. Congress and "only Congress can change it." Explore → You are here: Home / education / Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Research Grant (Sweden) Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Research Grant (Sweden) Subscribe to our Free Email Newsletter Now JOIN Deadline: 15-Sep-2026 The Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus provides rapid-response research funding for researchers addressing urgent scientific questions linked to current or potential outbreaks of hantavirus or Ebola virus. Grants of SEK 500,000 to SEK 2 million are available for one-year projects that can generate actionable evidence to support outbreak control, pandemic preparedness, and future prevention. What Is the Emergency Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Grant? The emergency call is part of Sweden’s national research programme in viruses and pandemics. It is designed to support research that responds quickly to emerging or ongoing virus-related threats with pandemic potential. The programme focuses on research that can produce results that are: Rapidly generated. Scientifically robust. Relevant to urgent outbreak questions. Applicable to real-world health and preparedness efforts. Capable of being translated into practice. The call specifically targets research related to hantavirus or Ebola virus. What Research Areas Are Supported? Projects can address urgent research questions across several academic disciplines. Eligible fields include: Humanities and social sciences. Clinical therapy research. Medicine and health. Natural and engineering sciences. Educational sciences. Research proposals should demonstrate a clear connection to urgent virus or pandemic-related challenges and explain how the expected findings could be implemented or used in practice. Funding Available Successful projects can receive: Minimum grant: SEK 500,000. Maximum grant: SEK 2,000,000. Project duration: One year. The funding is intended for rapid-response research rather than long-term projects that cannot produce relevant results within the one-year period. Why the Grant Matters Virus outbreaks can create urgent knowledge gaps that require rapid scientific investigation. This funding opportunity aims to support research that can help: Improve understanding of hantavirus and Ebola virus. Respond to ongoing or potential outbreaks. Limit disease transmission and consequences. Strengthen pandemic preparedness. Improve future outbreak prevention. Generate evidence that can be translated into practical action. Who Is Eligible? The call is targeted at individual researchers who meet specific Swedish Research Council grant requirements. Applicants must: Currently hold, or have previously held, a Swedish Research Council grant. Have a previous grant whose grant period ended in 2022 or later. Apply together with a Swedish higher education institution or another approved Swedish organisation. Ensure that the project leader is employed by the administrating organisation for at least 20% of a full-time equivalent during the grant period. Up to six additional researchers with a doctoral degree or equivalent qualification may participate. These participating researchers do not necessarily need to be employed by a Swedish institution. Administrating Organisation Requirement The application must be submitted in cooperation with an eligible Swedish higher education institution or another approved Swedish organisation that acts as the administrating organisation. The project leader must maintain employment with this organisation at a minimum level of 20% of full-time equivalent during the grant period. How to Apply 1. Confirm Your Eligibility Check that you currently hold or previously held a Swedish Research Council grant and that the end year of the relevant grant period was 2022 or later. 2. Identify an Eligible Swedish Organisation The application must be submitted together with a Swedish higher education institution or another organisation approved to administer the grant. 3. Develop a Rapid-Response Research Project The proposal should clearly identify an urgent research question related to hantavirus or Ebola virus. Explain: The problem being addressed. Why the research is urgent. The proposed methodology. Expected results. How quickly results can be generated. How findings could be translated into practice. How the project could contribute to outbreak response or pandemic preparedness. 4. Assemble the Research Team The project can include up to six additional researchers who hold a doctoral degree or equivalent qualification. Researchers outside Sweden may participate if they meet the relevant requirements. 5. Submit the Application in Prisma Applications must be submitted through Prisma by the stated deadline. After the call closes, the administrating organisation must sign the application in Prisma within seven calendar days. 6. Confirm Institutional Approval Applicants should coordinate with their administrating organisation well before submission to ensure that institutional requirements and the post-deadline signing process are completed on time. What Makes a Strong Proposal? A competitive proposal should demonstrate that the research can respond to an urgent virus-related knowledge need. Important elements include: A clearly defined hantavirus or Ebola research question. Strong scientific rationale. A realistic one-year workplan. Rapid and practical research outputs. Clear potential for real-world application. Relevance to outbreak response or pandemic preparedness. Appropriate expertise within the research team. A credible pathway from research findings to implementation. Common Mistakes to Avoid Applicants should avoid: Proposing research unrelated to hantavirus or Ebola virus. Designing a project that cannot reasonably be completed within one year. Failing to demonstrate the urgency of the research. Applying without the required Swedish Research Council grant history. Forgetting the requirement for a Swedish administrating organisation. Failing to meet the 20% employment requirement for the project leader. Submitting without allowing enough time for institutional signing. Missing the seven-calendar-day signing period after the call closes. Providing insufficient explanation of how research findings could be applied in practice. Key Details at a Glance Programme: Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Country: Sweden Funder: Swedish Research Council Research focus: Hantavirus and Ebola virus Minimum grant: SEK 500,000 Maximum grant: SEK 2,000,000 Project duration: 12 months Eligible disciplines: Humanities and social sciences, clinical therapy research, medicine and health, natural and engineering sciences, and educational sciences Lead applicant: Individual researcher with qualifying Swedish Research Council grant history Institutional requirement: Swedish higher education institution or approved Swedish organisation Additional researchers: Up to six Application system: Prisma Post-deadline signing: Within seven calendar days after the call closes Frequently Asked Questions Who can apply for the Emergency Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Grant? Individual researchers who currently hold or have previously held a Swedish Research Council grant may apply, provided the relevant grant period ended in 2022 or later and all other eligibility conditions are met. How much funding is available? Projects can request between SEK 500,000 and SEK 2,000,000. How long can the project last? The grant supports a one-year research project. Which viruses are covered by the emergency call? The call specifically supports urgent research related to hantavirus or Ebola virus with pandemic potential. Can researchers from outside Sweden participate? Yes. Up to six additional researchers with a doctoral degree or equivalent qualification can participate, and these researchers do not need to be employed by a Swedish institution. Does the applicant need a Swedish institution? Yes. The applicant must apply together with a Swedish higher education institution or another approved Swedish organisation, which serves as the administrating organisation. What happens after the application deadline? The administrating organisation must sign the application in Prisma within seven calendar days after the call closes. Applicants should therefore coordinate with their institution before the submission deadline. Conclusion The Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus provides targeted funding for researchers who can rapidly investigate urgent virus-related questions and translate findings into practical action. With grants of up to SEK 2 million for one-year projects, the opportunity is particularly relevant to eligible Swedish Research Council grant holders developing research that can strengthen outbreak response, limit health impacts, improve pandemic preparedness, and help prevent future virus-related crises. For more information, visit Swedish Research Council. Key Details at a Glance Programme: Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Country: Sweden Funder: Swedish Research Council Research focus: Hantavirus and Ebola virus Minimum grant: SEK 500,000 Maximum grant: SEK 2,000,000 Project duration: 12 months Eligible disciplines: Humanities and social sciences, clinical therapy research, medicine and health, natural and engineering sciences, and educational sciences Lead applicant: Individual researcher with qualifying Swedish Research Council grant history Institutional requirement: Swedish higher education institution or approved Swedish organisation Additional researchers: Up to six Application system: Prisma Post-deadline signing: Within seven calendar days after the call closes Frequently Asked Questions Who can apply for the Emergency Hantavirus or Ebola Virus Grant? Individual researchers who currently hold or have previously held a Swedish Research Council grant may apply, provided the relevant grant period ended in 2022 or later and all other eligibility conditions are met. How much funding is available? Projects can request between SEK 500,000 and SEK 2,000,000. How long can the project last? The grant supports a one-year research project. Which viruses are covered by the emergency call? The call specifically supports urgent research related to hantavirus or Ebola virus with pandemic potential. Can researchers from outside Sweden participate? Yes. Up to six additional researchers with a doctoral degree or equivalent qualification can participate, and these researchers do not need to be employed by a Swedish institution. Does the applicant need a Swedish institution? Yes. The applicant must apply together with a Swedish higher education institution or another approved Swedish organisation, which serves as the administrating organisation. What happens after the application deadline? The administrating organisation must sign the application in Prisma within seven calendar days after the call closes. Applicants should therefore coordinate with their institution before the submission deadline. Conclusion The Emergency Call for Hantavirus or Ebola Virus provides targeted funding for researchers who can rapidly investigate urgent virus-related questions and translate findings into practical action. With grants of up to SEK 2 million for one-year projects, the opportunity is particularly relevant to eligible Swedish Research Council grant holders developing research that can strengthen outbreak response, limit health impacts, improve pandemic preparedness, and help prevent future virus-related crises. For more information, visit Swedish Research Council. About NETEC What We Offer Educational Materials, Courses & Training We offer courses and training for nurses, physicians, emergency responders, and other health care professionals. Our resources provide facilities and individuals with preparedness best practices. Consultations & Support Services We can help health care facilities and EMS agencies prepare for special pathogen events with free virtual and onsite readiness consulting and assessments. Research Policies & Procedures Our network provides researchers with training, tools, and resources to quickly understand clinical syndromes and study effective treatments and clinical management strategies. Ask Our Experts Your organization can submit any question related to special pathogen response. Inquiries range from questions about PPE, to requests to review written protocols, to onsite visits for observing exercises and drills. New Podcast Inside the National Quarantine Unit: Preparedness, Partnership, and People Go inside the National Quarantine Unit (NQU) with experts from University of Nebraska Medical Center – UNMC/Nebraska Medicine as they discuss the unit’s recent activation following the MV Hondius Andes hantavirus response. Listen Upcoming Webinar Practical PPE Training Strategies for Special Pathogens Preparedness Join NETEC on September 8 at 12 p.m. ET for Practical PPE Training Strategies for Special Pathogens Preparedness, a webinar focused on helping healthcare organizations develop, implement, and sustain effective PPE training programs for frontline personnel. news.content: Features Videos Podcasts Specials Articles Shorts Donate English Español (Spanish) Français (French) Bahasa Indonesia (Indonesian) Brasil (Portuguese) India (English) हिंदी (Hindi) বাংলা (Bengali) Swahili Videos Podcasts Articles Short News Feature Stories The Latest Explore All Patricio Segura, journalist who defended Patagonia’s rivers, died of hantavirus, aged 54 Rhett Ayers Butler 23 Aug 2026 Chile Founder's briefs Comments Share article Share this article If you liked this story, share it with other people. Facebook Linkedin Threads Whatsapp Reddit Email Page link The fight to stop five dams on the Baker and Pascua rivers began in one of Chile’s least populous regions, far from Santiago, where national energy policy was set. HidroAysén said Chile needed the project to meet rising demand for electricity. Patricio Segura, working from Aysén in Chilean Patagonia, spent years picking apart that case. He read the filings, explained what the reservoirs and transmission lines would mean on the ground, and helped residents prepare their own arguments. The dams were never built. There was an obvious complication: Segura was also one of the organizers. Through the Corporación Privada para el Desarrollo de Aysén, or CODESA, he helped organize local opposition and worked on communications for Patagonia Sin Represas. International groups eventually joined, helping make the Baker and Pascua global symbols of river defense. Segura welcomed the wider audience but repeatedly insisted that decisions stay with the people who lived in Aysén. Born in Iquique, he studied journalism at the Universidad Católica del Norte and arrived in Coyhaique in 1995. He wrote about science, tourism, corruption, and politics. His reporting appeared in local outlets and national publications, and for 15 years he contributed investigations and columns to Patagon Journal. HidroAysén’s defeat left plenty else for him to cover. Salmon companies were spreading through the Patagonian fjords, leaving pollution and damaged seabeds while gaining political clout. Mines closed or changed hands without adequately addressing contaminated sites. Rural estates were divided into hundreds of speculative plots, or megaloteos, creating settlements outside normal planning and the provision of public services. Segura examined the permits and court cases, checked company claims, and named the officials responsible. Conservation groups did not escape his scrutiny. Segura objected when wealthy outsiders acquired land or promoted protected areas without giving local communities a meaningful role. In a three-part series, he described private conservation, tourism, and rural subdivision as “green Monopoly.” Protecting Patagonia, he argued, did not give philanthropists the right to decide its future. “What cannot happen,” he once said, “is for outsiders to dictate how things should be.” He believed conservation imposed from elsewhere could reproduce the inequalities of industrial development, and said so even when it meant criticizing his own movement. Segura did not mind giving offense, but he did his homework. In a column on salmon farming, a comparison with Mr. Burns’s control of Springfield in The Simpsons came only after a labor study, a diver’s death, and a Supreme Court ruling. His longer investigations worked the same way, drawing on official minutes, correspondence, company statements, and residents’ testimony. Allies received the same treatment when he thought they were wrong. Segura died from hantavirus on August 21st, aged 54. Less than a month earlier, Patagon Journal published his last column, “The Other AI: Ancestral Intelligence.” It examined knowledge built over generations of observation by Indigenous peoples, long dismissed as superstition. Segura believed that dismissal had done lasting damage. For him, that history contained “a lesson we need to reclaim.” Header image: Patricio Segura. news.content_zh: 以捍卫巴塔哥尼亚河流而闻名的记者帕特里西奥·塞古拉 (Patricio Segura) 于 2026 年 8 月 21 日死于 汉坦病毒,享年 54 岁。他的死亡得到了消息人士的证实,据报道,他一直在智利巴塔哥尼亚艾森积极参与环保倡导活动。塞古拉的工作重点是水坝、鲑鱼养殖和土地分割等问题,他是当地反对 HidroAysén 项目的关键人物。他的最后一篇专栏于 2026 年 8 月 27 日发表,讨论了祖先知识在保护工作中的重要性。尽管证据中没有详细说明更广泛的公共卫生影响或反应,但死亡凸显了汉坦病毒对个人的影响。消息来源证实了死因,但没有提供有关病毒传播或卫生系统影响的进一步细节。

analysis_zh.event: 记者帕特里西奥·塞古拉 (Patricio Segura) 因汉坦病毒去世,享年 54 岁。死亡经消息人士证实,死因直接归因于病毒。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: Segura 的死亡是一个单一事件,没有报告病例、死亡或普通人群中与汉坦病毒相关的暴露。证据中没有明确说明风险级别。

news.content: 10 10.8K Advertisement|Remove ads. One U.S. citizen has tested mildly positive for the Andes strain of hantavirus, U.S. health officials said Sunday. Moderna headquarters, exterior view, Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA. (Photo by: Plexi Images/GHI/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images) - Moderna confirmed on Friday that it has been pursuing early-stage research into mRNA-based vaccines against hantaviruses. - Bloomberg reported on Friday that Moderna’s hantavirus research is “early-stage and ongoing” and began well before the cruise-ship cluster was identified. - No hantavirus vaccine is currently approved anywhere in the world, and human clinical trials for Moderna’s candidates have not yet begun. Shares of Moderna (MRNA) rose as much as 7% on Monday before paring all gains after an American citizen was diagnosed with a hantavirus infection, for which the firm is reportedly developing a vaccine. One U.S. citizen has tested mildly positive for the Andes strain of hantavirus, U.S. health officials said Sunday. The asymptomatic passenger was one of 17 Americans repatriated from the hantavirus-stricken MV Hondius luxury cruise ship and was transported in a biocontainment unit upon arrival in Nebraska early Monday for monitoring at the University of Nebraska Medical Center’s biocontainment facility. A second American on the same flight is showing mild symptoms but has not yet been confirmed positive, according to the Department of Health and Human Services. Shares of the vaccine maker closed down 3% on Monday, likely due to investors taking profits after the stock rising 20% last week. The company has conducted preclinical work on hantaviruses in collaboration with the U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID) and is partnering with the Vaccine Innovation Center at Korea University College of Medicine through its mRNA Access Program to develop a potential immunization, the report said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MRNA jumped from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, while message volume increased from ‘high’ to ‘extremely high’ levels. A Stocktwits user pinned the drop in share price on Monday to profit-taking. Another user said that they bought the shares, hoping that the virus spreads in the coming weeks. MRNA stock has more than doubled over the past 12 months. In this photo illustration, the AST SpaceMobile (Space Mobile) logo is seen displayed on a smartphone screen. (Photo Illustration by Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) - Reports Q1 loss of $0.66 per share against expectations of $0.23 loss per share. - Revenue came in at $14.7 million amid expectations of $39 million. - Three out of 10 analysts rate ASTS a ‘buy’, five ‘hold’, and two ‘sell’. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) share price tumbled 11% after-hours after the company’s first quarter (Q1) revenue and earnings failed to meet expectations on the back of its plan to launch a fleet of 45 satellites by the end of 2026. The company, which is building the first space-based cellular broadband network, reported a loss of $0.66 per share on sales, compared to analyst forecasts of a $0.23 per-share loss. Revenue came in at $14.7 million, much lower than the $39 million analysts had expected. AST reported a loss of $0.20 a share and revenue of $718,000 in the same quarter last year. AST maintained full-year revenue guidance of between $150 million and $200 million, with the average Wall Street projections for 2026 revenue of $177 million. Wall Street projects ASTS to turn profitable in 2028 when annual sales hit $1.6 billion. “AST SpaceMobile is accelerating manufacturing, regulatory progress, commercial partnerships, and government programs, furthering our position as the only technology positioned to capture the massive direct-to-device broadband opportunity in full,” Abel Avellan, AST SpaceMobile’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said in a statement. Investors have grown keen on the space economy stocks, especially amid expectations of SpaceX’s IPO sometime later this year. AST expects to end 2026 with 45 satellites in orbit. “We have a robust global spectrum portfolio, the industry’s largest global commercial ecosystem, and a fortress balance sheet, positioning us for success as we create the space-based cellular broadband market,” Avellan added. The company’s BlueBird 8, BlueBird 9, and BlueBird 10 satellites were set for delivery to Cape Canaveral and an expected orbital launch in mid-June on SpaceX’s Falcon 9 launch vehicle. The Federal Communications Commission on April 22 granted the company ‘supplemental coverage authority’ to provide commercial services within the U.S. This regulatory milestone allows for direct-to-device broadband connectivity leveraging a planned network of up to 248 satellites. The firm’s strategic partners include Verizon, AT&T, and FirstNet. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was “extremely bullish” with “high” message volumes. One user was bullish for the long-term, citing more government contracts in the future. Three out of 10 analysts rate ASTS stock ‘buy’, five said ‘hold’, and two ‘sell’, as per data from Koyfin. The stock has dropped 15% over the past 12 months. Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital, sees Cisco's stock jumping to $110 to $120. - Target price of $120 signifies a near 22% upside from CSCO’s Monday closing price. - CSCO is expected to release its quarterly earnings on Wednesday after-hours. - 17 out of 26 analysts rate the stock ‘buy’ and nine rate ‘hold’. Cisco (CSCO) share price gained 2% on Monday and inched higher after-hours after NYSE insider Jay Woods released his target price on the stock ahead of the company’s earnings due later this week. Jay Woods, who was the New York Stock Exchange’s (NYSE) executive floor governor and currently the chief market strategist at Freedom Capital markets, expects the share price of the internet infrastructure company to rise to $110 or $120 over the next quarter as “realistic upside targets”, according to CNBC. Shares of Cisco closed at $98.7 on Monday. A price level of $120 would imply a rally of near 22%. The company reports earnings after Wednesday’s closing bell. “Cisco — a juggernaut back in the 90s, but hasn’t had that parabolic rise like it used to. Will it continue to rally into this strong tape? Right now it’s up 25% year to date, but last quarter they missed. Last quarter it was down 12% after a strong quarter, but people [were] concerned about the margins when it came to the memory spend,” said Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, told CNBC in an interview. Cisco has consistently beaten earnings and revenue estimates over the past 20 consecutive quarters, with investors moving their attention to the company’s shift from a hardware provider to one centered on AI infrastructure, cloud services, and software integration. In Q2 2026, Cisco delivered record-breaking results characterized by double-digit growth, reporting revenue of $15.35 billion, up 10% year-over-year, and adjusted earnings of $1.04 per share, both of which exceeded analyst expectations. Cisco reported a massive 65% jump in orders from cloud customers and booked $2.1 billion in AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers during the quarter. For Q3 2026, analysts expect revenues of $15.82 billion and earnings of $1.07 per share, as per data from Fiscal.ai, with investors looking for commentary on the plan to fulfill the $2 billion order flow amid supply constraints. 17 out of 26 analysts rate the stock ‘buy’ and nine rate ‘hold’, as per Koyfin data. One user expressed bullishness by saying CSCO could hit $120 per share following a strong quarterly performance and robust guidance. The stock has gained 16% over the past 12-months. Tesla Optimus humanoid robot on display inside the Tesla pop-up store near Shibuya crossing. (Photo by Stanislav Kogiku/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) - The analyst considered Tesla’s 17 product lines, ranging from vehicles and energy storage to supercharging, in-house insurance, FSD subscriptions, and the robotaxi business, but without Optimus. - Separately, Bloomberg reported earlier on Monday that President Donald Trump is expected to be joined by Tesla CEO Elon Musk on his official visit to China this week. - The move is aimed at strengthening business ties, securing trade deals, and advancing U.S. commercial interests amid ongoing tensions between the two economic powers. Shares of Tesla Inc. (TSLA) rose 4% on Monday after Piper Sandler analyst Alexander Potter said that near current prices, the EV giant is getting the Optimus business for free amid enthusiasm for CEO Elon Musk’s visit to China this week. Potter said in a note that, according to the firm’s analysis, Tesla is worth around $400 per share, but Optimus is not part of that analysis. The analyst considered Tesla’s 17 product lines, ranging from vehicles and energy storage to supercharging, in-house insurance, FSD subscriptions, and the robotaxi business, but without Optimus, according to a report from Yahoo Finance. “Critically, this analysis excludes Optimus, Tesla’s forthcoming humanoid robot,” Potter wrote. “In other words, at $400/share, we think investors can buy Optimus for free.”Optimus is one of Tesla’s thesis-defining products that will arguably be worth more than Tesla’s other businesses combined, the analyst said. However, valuing the business is difficult, the analyst said, while reiterating their $500 price target. Piper’s price target assumed $100 per share for Optimus as well as all other Tesla businesses not included in its analysis. The analyst admitted that this is far too low, according to the report from Yahoo Finance. Tesla said in January that the company would unveil the Optimus version meant for mass production, nicknamed Gen 3, in the first quarter. The company, however, is yet to hold the event. In April, Tesla CEO Elon Musk pinned the delay in revealing the production version of the Optimus humanoid robot to copycat fears. Musk said in the company’s Q1 earnings call that the company expects to reveal the robot closer to production in the July-August timeframe. The version slated for production is “almost ready to demonstrate,” minus some aesthetic elements, Musk said, while adding that he wants the version to be “polished” and working functionally. Tesla initially plans to manufacture Optimus on a production line that replaces its current one for the Model X and S at its Fremont factory. The last vehicles will be rolled off the final production line in early May. Following the retirement of the vehicles, Tesla will dismantle the old production line and install a new one, which Musk expects to take “at least a few months.” Musk also added that it is “literally impossible to predict” the production rate of the Optimus this year, owing to the new nature of the product and the intricacies of the supply chain involved. In April, Musk assured that Tesla would have an official ceremony to mark the end of Model S and X production. However, the company has yet to hold an event. Separately, Bloomberg reported earlier on Monday that President Donald Trump is expected to be joined by Tesla CEO Elon Musk on his official visit to China this week. The White House has invited Musk, along with Apple CEO Tim Cook and more than a dozen other top U.S. executives from companies including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and Boeing, to accompany him for high-stakes summit talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. The move is aimed at strengthening business ties, securing trade deals, and advancing U.S. commercial interests amid ongoing tensions between the two economic powers, the report said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock rose from bullish to extremely bullish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at normal levels. A Stocktwits user voiced optimism for Musk’s upcoming China trip, bringing positive momentum for the company by placing “Tesla directly in the middle of the U.S.-China trade and AI discussion.” Another said that many don’t understand the magnitude of the upcoming trip. Celsius Holdings (CELH) stock tumbled about 9% on Monday, and was on track to record its worst day in nearly six months following price target cuts from Morgan Stanley earlier on Friday last week. Morgan Stanley analyst Eric Serotta lowered the firm's price target on CELH to $55 from $64 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating on the shares. Serotta sees a path to improving the Celsius brand, but also sees slowing Alani momentum. Simultaneously, JPMorgan analyst Andrea Teixeira raised the firm's price target on Celsius to $70 from $67 and kept an ‘Overweight’ rating on the shares, and Roth Capital analyst Sean McGowan lowered the firm's price target on Celsius to $65 from $67 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares. McGowan also highlighted in a note that higher aluminum and freight costs are likely to slow the pace of margin expansion. Celsius Holdings, known for its fitness-focused energy drinks, made a range of acquisitions in April last year, including Alani Nu and Rockstar Energy. While Celsius and Alani Nu target wellness-conscious "new-age" drinkers, Rockstar provides a footprint in the classic energy sector, helping the company compete directly with giants like Monster and Red Bull. While CELH posted record revenues in its quarter ending March 2026, most of the growth came from its Alani Nu and Rockstar acquisitions, while sales of its core Celsius energy drink grew a mere 6%, raising investor concerns. However, much of the revenue growth came after CELH moved its Alani and Rockstar brands into the PepsiCo distribution system in August 2025, which drastically increased shelf space in convenience stores and international markets. CELH reported a record quarterly revenue of $782.6 million, representing 138% year-over-year growth, while also beating analyst expectations with adjusted earnings per share of $0.41, versus the forecasted $0.30 for its quarter ending March. However, most of the growth has come from sales of the newly acquired Alanu Nu and Rockstar Energy acquisitions, both of which are dilutive to gross margins. Celsius Holdings reported a consolidated gross margin of 48.3% in Q1’26, which was about 400 basis points lower than its margins in the same quarter last year. The core Celsius brand remains the highest-margin product, historically operating in the low-to-mid 50% range. Alani Nu and Rockstar have been identified by CELH management as a "lower margin profile" than the core Celsius brand. Alani Nu contributed to the 400-basis-point dip in overall consolidated margins. Cerebras Systems, the semiconductor startup challenging Nvidia’s (NVDA) dominance in the artificial intelligence chip market, on Monday raised the target price range for its initial public offering, signaling robust investor appetite for AI infrastructure. Cerebras is looking to list at $150 to $160 per share, according to a Monday filing, up from the $115 to $125 range it disclosed last week. With the updated IPO price range, Cerebras is set to generate as much as $4.8 billion in capital. This move brings the company's potential fully diluted market valuation to $48.8 billion, a significant jump from the $23 billion valuation established during its funding round in February. The company is preparing to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "CBRS" as early as May 14. Cerebras has positioned itself as a primary alternative to Nvidia by offering an AI hardware architecture separate from what Nvidia offers. Its flagship "Wafer-Scale Engine" is a single, massive chip the size of a dinner plate, designed to handle the immense computational requirements of large language models more efficiently than clusters of traditional processors. Financial disclosures included in Monday’s filing show revenue of $270.3 million for the first nine months of 2025, a significant jump from the $75.2 million reported during the same period a year earlier. Shares of Moderna (MRNA) rose as much as 7% on Monday before paring all gains after an American citizen was diagnosed with a hantavirus infection, for which the firm is reportedly developing a vaccine. One U.S. citizen has tested mildly positive for the Andes strain of hantavirus, U.S. health officials said Sunday. The asymptomatic passenger was one of 17 Americans repatriated from the hantavirus-stricken MV Hondius luxury cruise ship and was transported in a biocontainment unit upon arrival in Nebraska early Monday for monitoring at the University of Nebraska Medical Center’s biocontainment facility. A second American on the same flight is showing mild symptoms but has not yet been confirmed positive, according to the Department of Health and Human Services. Shares of the vaccine maker closed down 3% on Monday, likely due to investors taking profits after the stock rising 20% last week. The company has conducted preclinical work on hantaviruses in collaboration with the U.S. Army Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRIID) and is partnering with the Vaccine Innovation Center at Korea University College of Medicine through its mRNA Access Program to develop a potential immunization, the report said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around MRNA jumped from ‘bullish’ to ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours, while message volume increased from ‘high’ to ‘extremely high’ levels. A Stocktwits user pinned the drop in share price on Monday to profit-taking. Another user said that they bought the shares, hoping that the virus spreads in the coming weeks. MRNA stock has more than doubled over the past 12 months. AST SpaceMobile (ASTS) share price tumbled 11% after-hours after the company’s first quarter (Q1) revenue and earnings failed to meet expectations on the back of its plan to launch a fleet of 45 satellites by the end of 2026. The company, which is building the first space-based cellular broadband network, reported a loss of $0.66 per share on sales, compared to analyst forecasts of a $0.23 per-share loss. Revenue came in at $14.7 million, much lower than the $39 million analysts had expected. AST reported a loss of $0.20 a share and revenue of $718,000 in the same quarter last year. AST maintained full-year revenue guidance of between $150 million and $200 million, with the average Wall Street projections for 2026 revenue of $177 million. Wall Street projects ASTS to turn profitable in 2028 when annual sales hit $1.6 billion. “AST SpaceMobile is accelerating manufacturing, regulatory progress, commercial partnerships, and government programs, furthering our position as the only technology positioned to capture the massive direct-to-device broadband opportunity in full,” Abel Avellan, AST SpaceMobile’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, said in a statement. Investors have grown keen on the space economy stocks, especially amid expectations of SpaceX’s IPO sometime later this year. AST expects to end 2026 with 45 satellites in orbit. “We have a robust global spectrum portfolio, the industry’s largest global commercial ecosystem, and a fortress balance sheet, positioning us for success as we create the space-based cellular broadband market,” Avellan added. The company’s BlueBird 8, BlueBird 9, and BlueBird 10 satellites were set for delivery to Cape Canaveral and an expected orbital launch in mid-June on SpaceX’s Falcon 9 launch vehicle. The Federal Communications Commission on April 22 granted the company ‘supplemental coverage authority’ to provide commercial services within the U.S. This regulatory milestone allows for direct-to-device broadband connectivity leveraging a planned network of up to 248 satellites. The firm’s strategic partners include Verizon, AT&T, and FirstNet. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was “extremely bullish” with “high” message volumes. One user was bullish for the long-term, citing more government contracts in the future. Three out of 10 analysts rate ASTS stock ‘buy’, five said ‘hold’, and two ‘sell’, as per data from Koyfin. Cisco (CSCO) share price gained 2% on Monday and inched higher after-hours after NYSE insider Jay Woods released his target price on the stock ahead of the company’s earnings due later this week. Jay Woods, who was the New York Stock Exchange’s (NYSE) executive floor governor and currently the chief market strategist at Freedom Capital markets, expects the share price of the internet infrastructure company to rise to $110 or $120 over the next quarter as “realistic upside targets”, according to CNBC. Shares of Cisco closed at $98.7 on Monday. A price level of $120 would imply a rally of near 22%. The company reports earnings after Wednesday’s closing bell. “Cisco — a juggernaut back in the 90s, but hasn’t had that parabolic rise like it used to. Will it continue to rally into this strong tape? Right now it’s up 25% year to date, but last quarter they missed. Last quarter it was down 12% after a strong quarter, but people [were] concerned about the margins when it came to the memory spend,” said Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, told CNBC in an interview. Cisco has consistently beaten earnings and revenue estimates over the past 20 consecutive quarters, with investors moving their attention to the company’s shift from a hardware provider to one centered on AI infrastructure, cloud services, and software integration. In Q2 2026, Cisco delivered record-breaking results characterized by double-digit growth, reporting revenue of $15.35 billion, up 10% year-over-year, and adjusted earnings of $1.04 per share, both of which exceeded analyst expectations. Cisco reported a massive 65% jump in orders from cloud customers and booked $2.1 billion in AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers during the quarter. For Q3 2026, analysts expect revenues of $15.82 billion and earnings of $1.07 per share, as per data from Fiscal.ai, with investors looking for commentary on the plan to fulfill the $2 billion order flow amid supply constraints. 17 out of 26 analysts rate the stock ‘buy’ and nine rate ‘hold’, as per Koyfin data. Shares of Tesla Inc. (TSLA) rose 4% on Monday after Piper Sandler analyst Alexander Potter said that near current prices, the EV giant is getting the Optimus business for free amid enthusiasm for CEO Elon Musk’s visit to China this week. Potter said in a note that, according to the firm’s analysis, Tesla is worth around $400 per share, but Optimus is not part of that analysis. The analyst considered Tesla’s 17 product lines, ranging from vehicles and energy storage to supercharging, in-house insurance, FSD subscriptions, and the robotaxi business, but without Optimus, according to a report from Yahoo Finance. “Critically, this analysis excludes Optimus, Tesla’s forthcoming humanoid robot,” Potter wrote. “In other words, at $400/share, we think investors can buy Optimus for free.”Optimus is one of Tesla’s thesis-defining products that will arguably be worth more than Tesla’s other businesses combined, the analyst said. However, valuing the business is difficult, the analyst said, while reiterating their $500 price target. Piper’s price target assumed $100 per share for Optimus as well as all other Tesla businesses not included in its analysis. The analyst admitted that this is far too low, according to the report from Yahoo Finance. Tesla said in January that the company would unveil the Optimus version meant for mass production, nicknamed Gen 3, in the first quarter. The company, however, is yet to hold the event. In April, Tesla CEO Elon Musk pinned the delay in revealing the production version of the Optimus humanoid robot to copycat fears. Musk said in the company’s Q1 earnings call that the company expects to reveal the robot closer to production in the July-August timeframe. The version slated for production is “almost ready to demonstrate,” minus some aesthetic elements, Musk said, while adding that he wants the version to be “polished” and working functionally. Tesla initially plans to manufacture Optimus on a production line that replaces its current one for the Model X and S at its Fremont factory. The last vehicles will be rolled off the final production line in early May. Following the retirement of the vehicles, Tesla will dismantle the old production line and install a new one, which Musk expects to take “at least a few months.” Musk also added that it is “literally impossible to predict” the production rate of the Optimus this year, owing to the new nature of the product and the intricacies of the supply chain involved. In April, Musk assured that Tesla would have an official ceremony to mark the end of Model S and X production. However, the company has yet to hold an event. Separately, Bloomberg reported earlier on Monday that President Donald Trump is expected to be joined by Tesla CEO Elon Musk on his official visit to China this week. The White House has invited Musk, along with Apple CEO Tim Cook and more than a dozen other top U.S. executives from companies including BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and Boeing, to accompany him for high-stakes summit talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. The move is aimed at strengthening business ties, securing trade deals, and advancing U.S. commercial interests amid ongoing tensions between the two economic powers, the report said. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around TSLA stock rose from bullish to extremely bullish territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at normal levels. A Stocktwits user voiced optimism for Musk’s upcoming China trip, bringing positive momentum for the company by placing “Tesla directly in the middle of the U.S.-China trade and AI discussion.” Another said that many don’t understand the magnitude of the upcoming trip. Celsius Holdings (CELH) stock tumbled about 9% on Monday, and was on track to record its worst day in nearly six months following price target cuts from Morgan Stanley earlier on Friday last week. Morgan Stanley analyst Eric Serotta lowered the firm's price target on CELH to $55 from $64 and maintained an ‘Overweight’ rating on the shares. Serotta sees a path to improving the Celsius brand, but also sees slowing Alani momentum. Simultaneously, JPMorgan analyst Andrea Teixeira raised the firm's price target on Celsius to $70 from $67 and kept an ‘Overweight’ rating on the shares, and Roth Capital analyst Sean McGowan lowered the firm's price target on Celsius to $65 from $67 and kept a ‘Buy’ rating on the shares. McGowan also highlighted in a note that higher aluminum and freight costs are likely to slow the pace of margin expansion. Celsius Holdings, known for its fitness-focused energy drinks, made a range of acquisitions in April last year, including Alani Nu and Rockstar Energy. While Celsius and Alani Nu target wellness-conscious "new-age" drinkers, Rockstar provides a footprint in the classic energy sector, helping the company compete directly with giants like Monster and Red Bull. While CELH posted record revenues in its quarter ending March 2026, most of the growth came from its Alani Nu and Rockstar acquisitions, while sales of its core Celsius energy drink grew a mere 6%, raising investor concerns. However, much of the revenue growth came after CELH moved its Alani and Rockstar brands into the PepsiCo distribution system in August 2025, which drastically increased shelf space in convenience stores and international markets. CELH reported a record quarterly revenue of $782.6 million, representing 138% year-over-year growth, while also beating analyst expectations with adjusted earnings per share of $0.41, versus the forecasted $0.30 for its quarter ending March. However, most of the growth has come from sales of the newly acquired Alanu Nu and Rockstar Energy acquisitions, both of which are dilutive to gross margins. Celsius Holdings reported a consolidated gross margin of 48.3% in Q1’26, which was about 400 basis points lower than its margins in the same quarter last year. The core Celsius brand remains the highest-margin product, historically operating in the low-to-mid 50% range. Alani Nu and Rockstar have been identified by CELH management as a "lower margin profile" than the core Celsius brand. Alani Nu contributed to the 400-basis-point dip in overall consolidated margins. (Photo Illustration by Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images) - Cerebras could be worth up to $48.8 billion based on the new price range. - Initially, Cerebras planned to sell 28 million shares at $115-$125, targeting $3.5 billion before investor interest boosted the offering. - Cerebras now plans to sell 30 million shares. Cerebras Systems, the semiconductor startup challenging Nvidia’s (NVDA) dominance in the artificial intelligence chip market, on Monday raised the target price range for its initial public offering, signaling robust investor appetite for AI infrastructure. Cerebras is looking to list at $150 to $160 per share, according to a Monday filing, up from the $115 to $125 range it disclosed last week. With the updated IPO price range, Cerebras is set to generate as much as $4.8 billion in capital. This move brings the company's potential fully diluted market valuation to $48.8 billion, a significant jump from the $23 billion valuation established during its funding round in February. The company is preparing to list its shares on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker symbol "CBRS" as early as May 14. Cerebras has positioned itself as a primary alternative to Nvidia by offering an AI hardware architecture separate from what Nvidia offers. Its flagship "Wafer-Scale Engine" is a single, massive chip the size of a dinner plate, designed to handle the immense computational requirements of large language models more efficiently than clusters of traditional processors. Financial disclosures included in Monday’s filing show revenue of $270.3 million for the first nine months of 2025, a significant jump from the $75.2 million reported during the same period a year earlier. The asymptomatic passenger was one of 17 Americans repatriated from the hantavirus-stricken MV Hondius luxury cruise ship and was transported in a biocontainment unit upon arrival in Nebraska early Monday for monitoring at the University of Nebraska Medical Center’s biocontainment facility. elements_zh.time: 周一,Moderna (MRNA) 股价上涨了 7%,之后在一名美国公民被诊断出感染汉坦病毒后回吐了所有涨幅,据报道该公司正在为此开发 疫苗。这名无症状乘客是从遭受汉坦病毒的 MV Hondius 豪华游轮遣返的 17 名美国人之一,周一早些时候抵达内布拉斯加州后,被转移到生物隔离装置中,在内布拉斯加州大学医学中心的生物隔离设施中进行监测。过去 12 个月里,mRNA 的库存增加了一倍多。
elements_zh.location_and_population: 一名美国公民的安第斯山脉汉坦病毒病毒检测呈轻度阳性。周一早些时候,该人抵达内布拉斯加州后,被转移到生物隔离装置中,在内布拉斯加州大学医学中心的生物隔离设施中进行监测。
elements_zh.event: 卫生官员报告称,一名美国公民的安第斯汉坦病毒病毒检测呈轻度阳性。Moderna 周五证实,它一直在针对基于 mRNA 的 疫苗 对抗汉坦病毒进行早期研究。该公司已与美国陆军传染病医学研究所 (USAMRIID) 合作开展汉坦病毒的临床前工作,并通过其 mRNA Access 计划与高丽大学医学院的 疫苗 创新中心合作,开发一种潜在的免疫疗法。
elements_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 汉坦病毒 疫苗 目前在世界任何地方都没有获得批准,Moderna 候选药物的人体临床试验尚未开始。该公司股价周一收盘下跌 3%,可能是由于投资者在上周股价上涨 20% 后获利了结。Moderna 的汉坦病毒研究处于“早期阶段且正在进行中”,早在游轮集群确定之前就开始了。
elements_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 据报道,Moderna 正在开发针对汉坦病毒的 疫苗,并与美国陆军传染病医学研究所 (USAMRIID) 和高丽大学医学院的 疫苗 创新中心合作进行临床前工作。这名无症状乘客被运送到内布拉斯加大学医学中心生物防护设施的生物防护装置中进行监测。该公司尚未开始其 疫苗 候选药物的人体临床试验。周一股价下跌的原因是投资者获利了结。

《“死亡邮轮”持续扩散!汉坦病毒已波及多国,多人死亡、全球紧急追踪》 新西兰新闻 华人号 2026-05-12 04:53 阅读量:6.6万+ 华人号:新西兰新闻 一艘原本驶向南极的豪华探险邮轮,如今却被全球媒体称为“死亡邮轮”。 随着汉坦病毒(Hantavirus)在MV Hondius号邮轮上的持续扩散,世界卫生组织(WHO)与多国卫生部门正展开紧急追踪。截至目前,已有多个国家报告确诊或疑似病例,至少3人死亡,全球卫生系统高度戒备。 这场突如其来的病毒危机,正让原本浪漫的南极之旅,演变成一场跨越大洲的公共卫生警报。 据了解,MV Hondius号为一艘荷兰籍探险邮轮。疫情爆发后,船上乘客和工作人员陆续在世界各地出现症状,其中部分人病情严重,甚至死亡。世卫组织最新数据显示,目前已有7例确诊病例,另有1例“可能病例”,同时还有多名密切接触者正在接受调查。 在所有病例中,荷兰成为受影响最严重的国家之一。 一对荷兰老年夫妇在南美旅行后登船,随后相继病逝。丈夫利奥·希尔佩鲁德于4月初出现症状,数日后死亡;妻子米里亚姆随后在飞往南非途中病情恶化,于医院离世,最终被确诊感染安第斯病毒株(Andes strain)。 更令人担忧的是,一名荷兰籍船医也已确诊感染,目前正在荷兰接受隔离治疗。 英国方面同样出现多例病例。两名英国男子已确认感染,其中一人一度进入重症监护室,另一人为船上导游。还有一名英国男子被列为“可能病例”,目前仍在等待实验室最终结果。 由于其所处岛屿位置偏远,英国甚至出动军方人员空投紧急医疗物资,事件引发国际社会高度关注。 德国、瑞士、法国、西班牙及美国也陆续报告相关病例。 其中,一名德国女性在船上发烧后发展成肺炎,于5月2日死亡,尸检确认感染安第斯病毒;瑞士一名乘客返回欧洲后检测阳性;法国卫生部门则证实,一名遣返女性病情在夜间迅速恶化。 美国卫生与公共服务部表示,从邮轮撤离的17名美国公民中,已有一人PCR检测呈轻度阳性,另一人出现轻微症状,目前均已被送往专业医疗机构观察治疗。 西班牙方面也确认,一名撤离乘客PCR检测阳性,但暂未出现症状。 专家指出,目前最令人担忧的,并不仅是现有病例,而是“潜伏期后的全球扩散风险”。 由于安第斯病毒株被认为具有罕见的人传人能力,而许多乘客已在多个国家间飞行转机,因此未来数周将成为关键观察期。卫生专家认为,5月19日前后,或许将显现这次疫情是否会进一步扩大传播。 目前,“洪迪乌斯”号邮轮已离开西班牙特内里费岛,驶往荷兰。船上的阴影,却仍笼罩在全球公共卫生系统之上。 一艘邮轮,多个国家,数千公里航线。 Hondius号邮轮上的持续扩散,世界卫生组织(WHO)与多国卫生部门正展开紧急追踪。截至目前,已有多个国家报告确诊或疑似病例,至少3人死亡,全球卫生系统高度戒备。 这场突如其来的病毒危机,正让原本浪漫的南极之旅,演变成一场跨越大洲的公共卫生警报。 据了解,MV Hondius号为一艘荷兰籍探险邮轮。疫情爆发后,船上乘客和工作人员陆续在世界各地出现症状,其中部分人病情严重,甚至死亡。世卫组织最新数据显示,目前已有7例确诊病例,另有1例“可能病例”,同时还有多名密切接触者正在接受调查。 在所有病例中,荷兰成为受影响最严重的国家之一。 一对荷兰老年夫妇在南美旅行后登船,随后相继病逝。丈夫利奥·希尔佩鲁德于4月初出现症状,数日后死亡;妻子米里亚姆随后在飞往南非途中病情恶化,于医院离世,最终被确诊感染安第斯病毒株(Andes strain)。 更令人担忧的是,一名荷兰籍船医也已确诊感染,目前正在荷兰接受隔离治疗。 英国方面同样出现多例病例。两名英国男子已确认感染,其中一人一度进入重症监护室,另一人为船上导游。还有一名英国男子被列为“可能病例”,目前仍在等待实验室最终结果。 由于其所处岛屿位置偏远,英国甚至出动军方人员空投紧急医疗物资,事件引发国际社会高度关注。 德国、瑞士、法国、西班牙及美国也陆续报告相关病例。 其中,一名德国女性在船上发烧后发展成肺炎,于5月2日死亡,尸检确认感染安第斯病毒;瑞士一名乘客返回欧洲后检测阳性;法国卫生部门则证实,一名遣返女性病情在夜间迅速恶化。 美国卫生与公共服务部表示,从邮轮撤离的17名美国公民中,已有一人PCR检测呈轻度阳性,另一人出现轻微症状,目前均已被送往专业医疗机构观察治疗。 西班牙方面也确认,一名撤离乘客PCR检测阳性,但暂未出现症状。 专家指出,目前最令人担忧的,并不仅是现有病例,而是“潜伏期后的全球扩散风险”。 由于安第斯病毒株被认为具有罕见的人传人能力,而许多乘客已在多个国家间飞行转机,因此未来数周将成为关键观察期。卫生专家认为,5月19日前后,或许将显现这次疫情是否会进一步扩大传播。 目前,“洪迪乌斯”号邮轮已离开西班牙特内里费岛,驶往荷兰。船上的阴影,却仍笼罩在全球公共卫生系统之上。 一艘邮轮,多个国家,数千公里航线。
